judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H 3045. It would create the crime of obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse, set penalties for it, and add it to the state's sex offender registry. The South Carolina House passed it 76-20. As of September 2026 the Senate had not voted on it, so it has not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H 3645. It would increase the number of weeks of paid parental leave that eligible state employees get when a child is born or adopted. The South Carolina House passed it 80-31. As of September 2026 the Senate had not voted on it, so it has not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H 3927. The bill, titled the Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity Act, would bar every state office, division and unit from running diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and would require decisions to rest on merit instead. The South Carolina House passed it 82-32. As of September 2026 the Senate had not voted on it, so it has not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H 4760. It would create new crimes and penalties for using abortion-inducing drugs, and would move mifepristone and misoprostol onto the state's Schedule IV controlled substance list. Simply possessing either drug would become a crime, with some exceptions. The South Carolina House passed it 76-28. As of September 2026 the Senate had not voted on it, so it has not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H 4764. It would require every law enforcement agency that runs a jail to sign an agreement with federal immigration authorities to help enforce federal immigration law. The state law enforcement division would have to train agencies doing that work. The South Carolina House passed it 84-26. As of September 2026 the Senate had not voted on it, so it has not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H 4767. It would ban noncompete clauses in doctors' employment contracts, treating them as void and against public policy because they get in the way of a patient's choice of doctor. A doctor who leaves a practice could keep treating their existing patients. The South Carolina House passed it 58-53. As of September 2026 the Senate had not voted on it, so it has not become law.
